title: Psychological Steering in LLMs: An Evaluation of Effectiveness and Trustworthiness
extended_summary:
This paper examines how large language models (LLMs) can be steered to express specific emotional states and personality traits, and how such steering affects downstream trustworthiness. The authors introduce PsySET, a benchmark designed to evaluate both the effectiveness of psychological steering and its side effects across emotion and personality domains. The central problem is that existing work on steering LLMs has been fragmented, often focusing on one method or one type of evaluation; this paper instead compares prompting, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and representation engineering under a unified framework.

The paper studies four LLMs and several steering strategies, including zero-shot prompting, few-shot prompting, descriptive prompting, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), and vector injection (VI). For emotion steering, it uses psychometric-style tasks such as self-report, word-fragment completion, autobiographical memory, and ambiguous-situation interpretation; for personality steering, it uses questionnaires and behavioral-style benchmarks. It also evaluates whether steering changes safety, truthfulness, fairness, privacy, and other trustworthiness dimensions. No human participant population is studied; the paper is an LLM evaluation benchmark rather than an educational intervention.

The main conclusion is that prompting, especially few-shot and descriptive prompting, is the most effective overall method for expressing targeted emotions and traits, though it offers limited fine-grained control over intensity. Vector injection can provide smoother intensity control but often harms text quality and robustness, while SFT is more stable and DPO performs worst on many tasks. The authors conclude that psychological steering is powerful but risky, because it can introduce unexpected side effects such as increased toxicity, reduced factual robustness, or fairness degradation, depending on the emotion or personality trait being induced.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark/evaluation paper rather than a K-12 intervention study. It is peer-reviewed research-like in structure, but it does not evaluate an educational treatment or produce learner outcome evidence under a causal design.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct educational impact is measured. The paper’s relevance is methodological for LLM control, not an instructional or learner-outcome intervention in education.

interventions.use_case: Benchmarking and comparing LLM psychological steering methods for emotion/personality control, including prompt engineering, supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and vector injection at inference time.
